Subject: NDx MAP — test artifacts and timelines for TTFT/QPS deliverables

Alex —

Per our MAP, we committed to a small performance evidence bundle showing TTFT (time-to-first-token), latency tails, and concurrency behavior for the inference configuration you care about. I’m proposing the following deliverables and timeline so we can get you everything procurement and the execs need for close: 

- Artifacts: CSV exports (per-request metrics, per-scenario summary), a 1-page exec slide, and a short slide appendix with charts (latency percentiles, QPS vs concurrency).
- Links: live dashboard snippet, raw CSV export, and a short demo recording if helpful.
- Environment note: tests run on our Dedicated replica (4x A100s), baseline model = open-model-v2-8b (8-bit quantized), batching disabled for TTFT runs.
- Timeline: test runs this week (Oct 7–9), internal QA & exporting Oct 10–11, delivery to you Oct 12 with a brief sync/exec readout week of Oct 12.

Can you confirm the required concurrency profiles (e.g., steady 10 qps, burst to 50 qps, 200 concurrent requests ramp) and any procurement timing constraints? Once confirmed, Karthik and Marissa will run the harness and I’ll pack the artifacts.

Attachments: MAP_requirements_checklist.txt (attached stub)

Thanks —
Soojin Lee

Soojin / Marissa —

Plan for the harness and packaging below (internal):

- Test matrix (runs Oct 8–10):
  * TTFT: 200 1:1 requests, no batching, measure median/p95/p99, record cold vs warm KV cache.
  * Throughput: sustained QPS runs at 10, 60, 100; 10-minute windows each.
  * Concurrency stress: ramp to 250 concurrent connections, monitor tail latency and error behavior.

- Runtime notes: 4x A100 nodes, model open-model-v2-8b (int8), KV cache enabled for throughput runs, continuous batching off for TTFT. Include note about kernel-selection (fp16 path) in the appendix.

- Exports: per-request CSV (timestamp, request_id, ttft_ms, latency_ms, status_code), aggregated summary CSV, and a slide deck: 1-page exec + 3 appendix slides (p95/p99 charts, throughput curve, concurrency breakdown).

Marissa — can you own the CSV exports and one-pager? I’ll run the stress profile and collect kernel/runtime metadata. Evelyn — please reserve a short slot for a quick exec readout and confirm calendar availability Oct 12 10:00–10:30 PT.

Onward,
Karthik
Head of Benchmarking | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodai.com>
To: Alex Kent <alex.kent@northstardynamics.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@northstardynamics.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: NDx — Performance evidence bundle (TTFT/QPS/concurrency) — delivery

Alex / Sarah —

Delivering the MAP performance bundle as promised. Summary first, artifacts and links below. Let me know if you want a short 15–20 minute exec readout — we penciled Oct 12 10:00 PT but happy to move.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
- We validated TTFT and tail-latency behavior on your target model/config. Median TTFT: 48 ms; p95 latency: 210 ms; p99 latency: 430 ms. At sustained 60 QPS the median token generation latency increased ~12% compared to 10 QPS; under a 250-concurrency stress run we observed graceful degradation at 220 concurrent requests with increased p99 error rates due to queue saturation (detailed notes below).

Key numbers (from aggregate CSV):
- Median TTFT: 48 ms
- p95 latency: 210 ms
- p99 latency: 430 ms
- Sustained throughput curve: 10 QPS -> 60 QPS (linear), ~100 QPS shows 1.6x CPU/GPU utilization with marginal latency impact; beyond 180 QPS latency tails steepen.

Notes & recommendations:
- For production SLOs we recommend p95 < 250 ms and a concurrency cap per client to avoid the queue-saturation path.
- Consider enabling small batching for stable high-throughput workloads to reduce unit cost without impacting TTFT for most requests.

Artifacts attached and links:
- Attachments: ndx_latency_results.csv; ndx_ttft_concurrency_charts.pdf; ndx_exec_one_pager.pptx
- CSV (per-request): attached (ndx_latency_results.csv) — columns: timestamp, request_id, ttft_ms, latency_ms, status_code, concurrency_tag
- Dashboard: https://redwood-dashboard.internal/ndx/nd-2026-q4-a/results (contains live percentiles and export buttons)
- HubSpot MAP record: https://hubspot.com/deals/ND-2026-Q4-A

Run environment (for audit): 4x NVIDIA A100, model open-model-v2-8b quantized int8, runtime kernel fp16 path selected for generation, tests run Oct 8–10. Full appendix in the attached PDF with charts and the raw CSV.

If this looks good I’ll open the DocuSign link for the PO and we can schedule a short exec readout for Oct 14 to close.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwoodai.com
